neet_che_u18_t01_1.working: Amine class depends on how many carbon groups are attached to N, not on the carbon type. In tert-butylamine, N carries one alkyl group and two H atoms, so it is a primary amine.

neet_che_u18_t01_2.working: The parent chain is ethanamine, and the second ethyl group sits on nitrogen. The name is therefore N-ethylethanamine.

neet_che_u18_t01_3.working: The C3H9N amines are propan-1-amine, propan-2-amine, N-methylethanamine and N,N-dimethylmethanamine. That gives 4 isomers.

neet_che_u18_t01_4.working: C6H5CH2NH2 is phenylmethanamine (III). H2N(CH2)6NH2 is hexane-1,6-diamine (IV). C6H5N(CH3)2 is N,N-dimethylbenzenamine (I). p-CH3OC6H4NH2 is p-anisidine (II).

neet_che_u18_t01_5.working: A is true: N is sp3 and the C-N-C angle is about 108°. B is false: in benzylamine N is bonded to CH2, not to the ring, so it is not an aryl amine. C is true: the lone pair delocalises into the ring. D is false: (CH3)4N+Cl- is a quaternary ammonium salt. E is true: class depends on the number of carbons bonded to N. So A, C and E are correct.
